LESSON: SELF- EXPRESSION

Grade: SNE  /  physical-impairment / PP1
Subject: General
Strand: Listening and Speaking
Topic 1.2: Self- expression
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 4

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Self- expression, part of Listening and Speaking in SNE  /  physical-impairment / PP1 General.

Key inquiry question: What kind of work would you like to do when you grow up?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. identify the appropriate titles of family members, ● Tell news about family members. Learners with speech difficulties could use alternative modes of communication to What kind of work would you like to do when you grow up? 23

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Self- expression in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Self- expression together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Creativity and imagination: Communication and self-expression as the learner tells stories about family members and the

work done by different members of the family.

• Self-efficacy: knowing my family as the learner tells who are the members of the family and the ones not.

• Citizenship is enhanced as the learner talks about and appreciates the roles and responsibilities of family members.

Values:
• Unity is developed as the learner appreciates the role played by each member of the family to keep them together.

• Social justice is enhanced as the leaner learns the importance of fairness in sharing work and responsibilities among family

members.

24

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
Socio-economic issues awareness where the learner understands that parents work in different places and earn differently.

Link to other Learning Areas: Self-expression is a life skill necessary in all learning areas for learners to answer questions in

class, for daily communications and for expression of needs.

Suggested learning resources: Charts, pictures showing family members
